title: Throughput lease orchestrator for zero-downtime upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Performing rolling upgrades and planned maintenance on Dedicated GPU fleets often causes transient SLO violations because capacity is temporarily reduced and KV-cache cold-starts increase p99 latency. Current drain logic does not express fine-grained throughput commitments, and autoscalers indiscriminately refill capacity which can lead to noisy neighbor artifacts across tenants.

Goal: Build a Throughput Lease Orchestrator (TLO) that issues time-bounded "leases" representing guaranteed throughput capacity for maintenance waves. The orchestrator coordinates node drains, warmup handoffs, autoscaler reservations, and KV-cache warming to achieve upgrades with negligible customer-visible latency spikes.

Scope: MVP covers Dedicated fleets only (non-shared tenancy), implements per-host lease negotiation, integrates with existing drain controllers, exposes a rollout API for Console, and produces telemetry for post-mortem analysis.

Out of scope for MVP: cross-region live migration, multi-tenant fairshare algorithms, and automatic hardware preemption.
tasks: Design lease schema and state machine (requested_capacity, guaranteed_capacity, start_ts, end_ts, priority)
Extend node drain controller to accept lease tokens and defer eviction until downstream handoff confirms capacity handover
Autoscaler integration: allocate provisional instances matching lease reservations and mark them as 'reserved' to avoid normal scale-to-zero churn
KV-cache warmup protocol: prefetch common prefixes and prime KV snapshots on replacement nodes before they start serving customer traffic
Console API: UI control for creating maintenance waves with target percentage of fleet and SLA profile
Telemetry: emit lease events, handoff latencies, cache-warmup success rates, and SLO delta per wave
Chaos test harness: simulate node failures and delayed warmups to validate graceful fallback policies
acceptance_criteria: Create/approve a maintenance wave in Console that reserves N% of fleet capacity via TLO
During a staged upgrade of 10% fleet, p95 latency does not exceed baseline by more than 10% and p99 remains within SLO for 95% of requests
Replacement nodes report KV-cache warmup status and at least 80% of targeted prefixes are primed before traffic cutover
Autoscaler honors provisional reservations for the duration of the lease and does not reclaim reserved instances prematurely
Rollout API supports abort/rollback and SLO-driven automatic pause if observed impact exceeds configured thresholds
comments: 2026-02-12 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting held with runtime, autoscaler, and console. Agreed on lease token format and conservative defaults for MVP.
2026-02-20 Oliver Grant: Prototype lease state machine implemented. Handoff handshake uses two-phase ack to avoid split-brain during concurrent waves.
2026-02-28 SRE: Load tests show KV warmup reduces cold-start tokens by ~65% for checkpointed prefixes. Need to expand prefix sampling.
2026-03-05 Design review: PM requested that Console expose per-customer emergency-exempt toggle for critical enterprise tenants.
2026-03-10 QA: Began chaos experiments; observed a pathological case where reserved autoscaler nodes were preempted by cloud spot reclaim. Added a guarded lease extension flow.
